notes.title: Demo update and Eastern Martial Artists Week
notes.notes:
[p]Hey, Kohan here - the programmer behind Disco Samurai,
[/p][p]Great news! - Because of the fact that we are participating in Eastern Martial Artists Week event and because we haven't updated for some time ("some time" here meaning almost a year...) we've decided that it's a great time to update the demo![/p][p][/p][h2]So - what's new?[/h2][p][/p][h3]New levels[/h3][p]Demo now features entire [b]chapter 1[/b] (out of 7 in full game). It now also includes [b]2 story levels[/b] where you can learn a little bit more about real-world life of the Fox. And on top of that you will also have an opportunity to take part in a [b]motorcycle chase[/b]![/p][p][/p][h3]Rhythm improvements[/h3][p]Rhythm is fundamental to our game... and It worked kinda meh before. So now we made a lot of improvements and fixes, including [b]fixing audio-video synchronization[/b] issues and [b]enchancing UI/UX[/b] - you can now see more things that react to the rhythm. But the most important change, I think, is [b]sound effects scheduling[/b] - it means that even if you perform action slightly to early the game will wait until it's the right time and it will play the sound effect on the beat! it really helps you to stay in the rhythm.[/p][p]And we've also added a [b]calibration screen[/b] - most of the time the game should work without calibration, but you might need to use it if you feel some delay (for example when playing on TV).[/p][p][/p][h3]Keychains (Perks)[/h3][p]You can now customize your playstyle! You do that by wearing keychains which provide you small bonuses - but before you can equip them you need to earn them. Each keychain has a challenge you need to complete in order to unlock that keychain.[/p][p][/p][h3]Polishing[/h3][p]There was a trillion changes in that department so I'll just share the most fun ones:[/p][list][*][p][b]Destructible environments[/b] - you can now destroy small parts of the environment - like chairs or glasses - It doesn't have any tactical meaning, It's just for fun.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Rhythmic environment[/b] - parts of the level now just move to the rhythm! Hopefully that also helps you keep up with the beat.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Enemies leave blood splatters[/b] - It makes the world feel just a little bit more interactive (and brutal).[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Custom music[/h3][p]And you can now use custom music in the game! However, you must first complete the level before you can play it with custom music. Please bear in mind, though, that the UI for custom music is still a work in progress.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]One final note - the demo now has a separate store page - which means you can leave a review![/p][p][/p][p]And that would be it for today - I hope you will try out the demo![/p]

notes.title: Demo update based on your feedback
notes.notes:
Hey, Kohan here - the programmer behind Disco Samurai,

Today I wanted to share with you some of the changes we made to the demo based on the feedback we received from you during Steam Next Fest.

Those changes include:
[list]
[*] Difficulty balance
[list]
[*] Rebalanced levels - we're making them a bit easier
[*] Enemies now have shorter attack range, allowing you to dash away if you're under pressure
[*] Enemies now show an indicator one beat before they start their attack sequence
[*] Enemies now attack more sparingly, allowing you to take more initiative between their combos
[*] Success window is now larger - so if you've got trouble keeping up with the rhythm it should help
[*] Both powers - kick and shooting - now cost the same amount of flow to keep flow management simpler[/list]
[*] Added "Restart level" button
[*] Added video tutorials in place of images
[*] Temporarily disabled calibration - currently it caused more problems than it resolved, but it will definitely be back for release
[*] If you've played previous demo version your progress will be reset
[*] Bug fixes and other small changes
[/list]
And while these changes in a large part make the game easier, please keep in mind that we still want our game to be challenging, but we definitely don't want it to be frustrating.

That's all from me - I hope you will have a blast on upcoming Rhythm Fest!

notes.title: Disco Samurai is a brutally difficult and brilliant Sekiro-like rhythm slasher
notes.notes:
Disco Samurai is a game that’s so difficult I’d have given up playing sooner if it didn’t contain so many of my absolute favourite action game things. Tense, decisive duels. Violence that’s both brutal and a little silly. Scalpel-sharp parry n' strike back-and-forths. Short stages that dole out chunky progression hits of dopamine, as quickly as they wrest those hits away from you with another humbling beatdown. Perhaps most importantly, it aims to do one thing - rhythm combat - and does it brilliantly. It's got teeth, but it's also got groove.
